For modular fee structure part-time courses: Annual Award Fee paid for a maximum of two years, Registration Fee and Dissertation Fee paid in full, and module fees for the minimum number of modules required
No separate application, nomination or extra documentation - consideration is automatic
Membership of the Clarendon scholar community of about 700 on-course scholars from around 70 nations

Applicants who hold a deferred graduate offer are not eligible to be considered
Current students who will continue to study for the same degree at Oxford in the next year are not eligible

An excellent academic record is essential - the majority of successful scholars usually have at least a first class honours degree or its equivalent, for example a GPA of at least 3.7 out of 4, or an outstanding academic record at Master's level

Meet the academic requirements of the course as well as the Clarendon selection criteria

Future potential and aptitude for the proposed course of study, assessed by reviewing references and research proposals

Study support grant for part-time scholars to assist with non-fee costs, worth a sixth, a third or half of the UKRI minimum doctoral stipend rate

official.application_route: Apply to your Oxford graduate course via the University's application form by the December or January deadline for that course; Clarendon consideration is automatic with no separate scholarship application.
official.study_mode: Full-time and part-time DPhil and Master's courses eligible; full-time scholars receive the living expenses grant, part-time scholars receive a study support grant
official.citizenship_residency: No restrictions by nationality or country of ordinary residence
official.international_eligibility: Open to all nationalities; course fees are covered in full for both Home and Overseas fee status students

official.description: The Clarendon Fund's purpose is to assist academically outstanding graduate students through their studies at the University of Oxford, making it the University's largest scholarship scheme with over 230 new awards in 2025/26. Like all fully-funded Oxford scholarships, it covers course fees and provides a grant for living expenses, with no quotas by nationality or degree and automatic consideration for every applicant to a degree-bearing graduate course by the relevant December or January funding deadline.
official.region: United Kingdom (University of Oxford); scholars come from around 70 nations
official.program_type: Merit-based graduate scholarship scheme covering all full-time and part-time DPhil and Master's courses

applicant_utility.summary: Clarendon is Oxford's flagship merit scholarship: apply to any full-time or part-time Master's or DPhil by the December or January deadline for that course and you are automatically considered - there is no separate form, essay or nomination to arrange. The award pays course fees in full for Home and Overseas students plus an annual living grant of at least the UKRI minimum stipend (£20,780 in 2025-26). In practice your course application is the scholarship submission, so the references, transcripts, statement of purpose and research proposal are what actually decide the money.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Applicants with a genuinely outstanding academic record - typically a first-class degree or equivalent such as a GPA of 3.7/4 or higher - in any subject, in any country, who want funding decided purely on academic merit.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your course's exact December or January funding deadline on its course page - miss it and you are outside Clarendon consideration entirely
Brief your two referees early and specifically, because departmental academics read references and research proposals when nominating scholars
Prepare an official transcript and check your classification or GPA against the stated first-class-equivalent guideline before applying
Do not hold or request a deferred offer - a deferred graduate offer removes you from consideration for this cycle
Watch your email into mid-June: successful candidates are contacted by email with the CB1 offer letter, most initial offers go out by the end of April, and unsuccessful applicants are never notified
common_rejection_risks: Missing the course's December or January funding deadline - there is no late route in
Picking a course whose deadline is March rather than December/January, which silently excludes you from Clarendon
Strong academics undermined by thin references or an unfocused statement of purpose, since motivation and future potential are explicitly assessed
Holding a deferred offer, or being a current Oxford student continuing the same degree next year - both are disqualifying
Assuming borderline cases can be rescued by extra documents or a nomination request; there is no mechanism for that
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Continuation charges levied after your period of fee liability, travel to Oxford, visa and immigration health surcharge costs, and anything above the living grant for a single student living in Oxford.
document_audit: The graduate application form is the entire submission - missing supporting documents leave the application incomplete and it will not be assessed by the department, let alone nominated
Oxford's Application Guide sets strict rules for transcripts, references and statements that can differ from what other UK universities ask of you
For research degrees, referees' reports carry the assessment of your research aptitude, so choose referees who can speak concretely to your proposed project
alerts: There is no separate scholarship application and no late window; the only thing you control is a complete, excellent course application by the December or January deadline
If you have not heard from the Clarendon Fund Administrator by mid-June, assume you were not awarded - late nominations happen only in summer if admitted scholars withdraw
Part-time applicants receive a study support grant worth a sixth, a third or half of the stipend rather than the full living grant, and coverage of modular fees is limited to compulsory components
College transfer may be required to take up a partnership award; scholars informed of a transfer cannot decline it
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the Oxford graduate application from the course page by the December or January deadline; departments nominate, divisions shortlist in February or March, and CB1 offer letters are emailed mostly by the end of April, followed by the CB2 funding breakdown letter.

official.deadline_central_display: December or January admissions deadline for your chosen course (see the course page)

Applications held over after the deadline to be re-evaluated against March-deadline applications, or placed on a waiting list, are not eligible for scholarship consideration.

The full cost of the individual Leadership Programme place
A one-year leadership development programme with philosophical discussions, business skills and communication training within a supportive community
Long-term mentoring and networking through the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust

You must be offered a place on an eligible course from the published list (the Trust confirms the scholarships fund a limited number of 1-year master-level courses and do not support applications for Doctorates/DPhil)
Not open to candidates who hold deferred offers to start in 2027-28
Students currently at Oxford are not eligible to apply unless they are already Weidenfeld-Hoffmann scholars

official.study_mode: Full-time only - applicants must be starting a new full-time graduate course at Oxford
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be ordinarily resident in one of the eligible countries published on the programme page (mainly developing and emerging economies)

official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Course must appear on the published eligible-courses list, which comprises around 50 one-year master's programmes (for example BCL, MBA, MJur, MPP, MSc African Studies, MSc Modern South Asian Studies, MSc Refugee and Forced Migration Studies, MSc Global Governance and Diplomacy); DPhil applications are not supported
official.duration: The full duration of fee liability for the agreed course (9-12 months for the one-year master's programmes funded), plus the Leadership Programme from mid-September to early July
official.description: The Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships and Leadership Programme cultivates the leaders of tomorrow by providing fully-funded graduate scholarships - 100% of course fees and a living costs grant of at least £21,805 - alongside a comprehensive programme of leadership development, long-term mentoring and networking. Established in 2015 and doubled in size in 2017 after a £9m donation from André Hoffmann matched by £6m from Oxford, it is part of the Oxford Graduate Scholarships matched-funding initiative, with the University contributing 40% of funds and donors to the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Trust 60%.
official.region: United Kingdom (University of Oxford); candidates mainly from developing and emerging economies
official.program_type: Fully-funded graduate scholarship with a leadership development programme, for listed one-year master's courses at Oxford

applicant_utility.summary: This is a leadership-tracked award rather than a pure academic contest: you must be ordinarily resident in one of the published eligible countries, be starting a new full-time one-year master's on the eligible-course list, and use a dedicated Scholarships Statement to show how your subject will improve public life back home. The route is a single Oxford graduate application with the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann programme selected in the Scholarships section plus the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement 2027/28 uploaded by your course's December or January deadline - one application, but one extra mandatory document. Shortlisted candidates interview online, likely in April 2027, and decisions are expected by the end of May 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Early-career professionals and outstanding graduates from eligible developing and emerging economies who intend to return home and can tie their field of study to a concrete public-impact career.
application_readiness_checklist: Check both published lists before drafting anything - the eligible-countries list and the eligible-courses list (around 50 one-year master's programmes); a non-listed course or residence outside the list makes the application ineligible regardless of merit
Download the Weidenfeld-Hoffmann Scholarships Statement 2027/28 from the programme page and upload it with the application before your course's deadline
Complete the 'Nationality and ordinary residence' section of the application form precisely, since Oxford uses exactly this data to assess country eligibility
Build the public-life narrative early: the connection between your subject, your longer-term career objectives and improving public life is the heart of both the Statement and the interview
Secure a passing English test score - the Trust states applicants must have passed the required English language test to be accepted onto the Programme
common_rejection_risks: Ordinary residence or nationality falling outside the published eligible-country list - the list is applied mechanically
Choosing a course not on the eligible list; the award funds listed one-year master's programmes only and does not support DPhil applications
Forgetting to select the programme in the University of Oxford Scholarships section, or not uploading the Statement by the deadline
A generic Statement that never ties the subject to returning home and improving public life in the country of origin or region
Holding a deferred 2027-28 offer, or being a current Oxford student who is not already a Weidenfeld-Hoffmann scholar - both are barred
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Flights and travel to Oxford, UK visa costs and the immigration health surcharge, and living costs above the £21,805 grant; family members cannot join these scholars as student dependants under current UK visa rules.
document_audit: The Scholarships Statement is a distinct, mandatory upload - an application without it is not considered even when the course application itself is excellent
The ordinary-residence details in the application form must be consistent with the Statement; contradictions are a credibility risk at interview
Course applications held over after the December/January deadline for March re-evaluation, or placed on a waiting list, lose scholarship eligibility entirely
alerts: Applying constitutes consent for your application to also be considered for the Trust's other schemes (Oxford Pakistan Programme and Chevening-Weidenfeld-Hoffmann), which are selected separately by the Trust
Successful candidates are transferred to a partner college to take up the scholarship, so college preference is not fully within your control
The award covers one-year master's courses only - DPhil applicants should consider Clarendon or other Oxford schemes instead
If you have not heard by the end of May 2027, assume the application was unsuccessful; no individual feedback is provided
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One graduate application: select the programme in the Scholarships section, upload the 2027/28 Statement by the course's December or January deadline, interview online if shortlisted in April 2027, with decisions by the end of May 2027.
